title: Trade or keep the tension?
outcomes: Chooses between trading and keeping the tension in unlabeled positions
Names which piece a trade gives up and which it removes
Reads the effect of one changed feature on whether a trade helps

steps.text:
In **Trades: which piece goes, which stays** you compared two trades. Now the choice is *whether to trade at all*.
A trade needs a purpose: remove an active piece, remove a defender, settle a point. A trade without one can give away your best-placed piece, or relieve a cramped opponent.
**Rule of thumb:** ask before each trade which of the two pieces matters more. The list of purposes is a guide, not a law.

Keeping the tension (leaving both pieces able to capture each other) is a move too. Before you capture, name the piece you give up and the piece you remove, and see how well each is placed.
The next three positions differ by a single feature. Predict each, then read the check. The engine's verdict is evidence at a fixed depth, not a proof.

steps.title: Same trade, one pawn fewer or one pawn moved
steps.prompt: White could take the knight on d7 in each position. Does the trade cost White at least 0.4 pawn compared with the engine's best move?
Before each of the last positions, did you ask what the trade gives up as well as what it removes? Which of the three did you get wrong, and what did you look at last?
